name: Campus AI Fouju
summary: Campus AI, a joint venture of the UAE fund MGX, French public bank Bpifrance, Mistral AI and NVIDIA, is developing a 1.4 GW AI data center campus at Fouju in Seine-et-Marne, about 40 km southeast of Paris. Plans call for roughly eleven data center buildings plus a training building on about 89 hectares, fed by a dedicated 400 kV substation. Environmental authorizations and the phase-one building permit were granted in summer 2026, phase-one works were scheduled from September 2026, and the first three data centers are targeted for early 2028. Local opponents have said they will appeal.

location.note: Nominatim centroid of the commune of Fouju; sources name the commune but not a parcel.

parties.name: Campus AI
parties.note: Joint venture that acquires land, builds high-voltage and shared infrastructure, and co-invests with data center developers; site companies Campus AI SPV1, SPV2 and SPV4 are authorized to operate DC1, DC2 and DC4.

parties.name: Mistral AI
parties.note: Described as the founding client, securing up to 200 MW of compute capacity with Campus AI (announced 2026-06-01; the source does not say all of it is at Fouju).

parties.name: Eiffage
parties.note: General contractor (consortium led by Eiffage Énergie Systèmes) for the 400/33 kV substation and shared infrastructure, contract above EUR 120 million.

parties.name: RTE
parties.note: Signed a fast-track grid connection agreement with Campus AI on 2026-01-26 and was authorized to build a substation at the site.

metrics.note: Final output rating of the 400/33 kV substation Eiffage is building; same headline figure as the campus capacity, not additional.
News report attributing the sum to MGX, NVIDIA, Mistral AI and Bpifrance; no company source opened for this figure.
Of which 73 hectares to be built on.
Data center buildings; a training center is additional.
First three data centers, plus a reception and training building and the substation, due early 2028.

milestones.note: Joint venture announced at the Choose France summit for an Île-de-France campus.
Start of the voluntary public pre-consultation under the CNDP framework (ran to 2025-11-23).
Fast-track grid connection agreement signed with RTE.
Single public inquiry opened (to 2026-05-30) covering environmental authorizations, local plan change and building permit.
At Choose France 2026 the joint venture said it plans up to 3 GW in France through a second, not yet named site that will complement the Fouju campus.
Eiffage named general contractor for the substation and shared infrastructure.
Approval of the Fouju local plan (PLU) amendment.
Prefectoral environmental authorizations for data centers and an RTE substation.
Start of phase-1 works as listed in the local authority's project timeline; archaeological excavations on 15 hectares were also under way from May 2026.
Early 2028 delivery of the first phase per the local timeline; the 2025 announcement targeted service by 2028.

power_sources.description: Fast-track connection to the RTE transmission grid through a new 400/33 kV substation rated for 1.4 GW at full build-out.

notes: Investment figures for the campus vary widely in public reporting; only the EUR 50 billion figure from an opened news source is recorded. A June 2026 announcement raised the joint venture's national target to up to 3 GW with an unnamed second site, which is not part of this record. Opponents (collective Stop IA à Fouju) said they would file an appeal against the authorizations.
